format: Text with inline TeX in $...$ and display TeX in $$...$$. Answer label and value fields are TeX without delimiters.

problems.title: Air onto glass at normal incidence
problems.prompt: A plane wave in air hits a glass surface ($\varepsilon_r=4$, $\mu_r=1$) at normal incidence. Find $\Gamma$, $\tau$, the standing-wave ratio in air, and the fractions of power reflected and transmitted.

problems.title: Checking power balance
problems.prompt: A $10\ \mathrm{V/m}$ plane wave in air hits a dielectric with $\varepsilon_r=9$ at normal incidence. Find the reflected and transmitted field amplitudes and the three average power densities, and check that power balances.
hints: $S_{\mathrm{av}}=|E|^2/(2\eta)$ in each medium, using that medium's $\eta$.

problems.title: Standing wave in front of a metal plate
problems.prompt: A $1\ \mathrm{GHz}$ plane wave with $E^i_0=5\ \mathrm{V/m}$ in air hits a perfectly conducting plate at $z=0$ at normal incidence. Write the total field in air, and find where it is zero and where it is largest.

problems.title: Radio waves into the sea
problems.prompt: A $1\ \mathrm{MHz}$ plane wave in air hits the sea ($\sigma=4\ \mathrm{S/m}$, $\varepsilon_r=81$) at normal incidence. Find $\eta_2$, $\Gamma$ and the fraction of power that enters the water.
hints: Seawater is a good conductor at 1 MHz: $\eta_c\approx(1+j)\sqrt{\pi f\mu/\sigma}$.
The power fraction that enters is $1-|\Gamma|^2$.
steps: Only about 1.0% of the power enters the sea, and that part dies within a few skin depths.

problems.title: Antireflection coating for a lens
problems.prompt: Glass has $n=1.5$. How much light (at normal incidence) reflects from bare glass in air? Design a single-layer antireflection coating for $\lambda_0=600\ \mathrm{nm}$: find its refractive index and thickness.
hints: The coating needs $n_2=\sqrt{n_1n_3}$ and a thickness of a quarter of the wavelength inside it.
steps: About 4% of the light reflects from each bare surface.

problems.title: Light entering water
problems.prompt: Light in air hits a still water surface ($n=1.33$) at $30^\circ$ from the normal. Find the angles of reflection and transmission.
steps: The wave bends toward the normal going into the denser medium.

problems.title: Critical angle of glass
problems.prompt: Light travels inside glass ($n=1.5$) toward a glass–air surface. Find the critical angle. What happens to a ray that arrives at $50^\circ$?
steps: $50^\circ>41.8^\circ$, so the ray is totally internally reflected. That is how a prism with $45^\circ$ faces works as a mirror.

problems.title: Acceptance angle of an optical fibre
problems.prompt: An optical fibre has a core with $n_f=1.52$ and cladding with $n_c=1.49$. Find the critical angle at the core–cladding boundary, the numerical aperture and the acceptance angle in air.
steps: Light entering the end face within this angle of the axis stays trapped in the core.

problems.title: Brewster angle of glass
problems.prompt: Find the Brewster angle for light going from air into glass ($n=1.5$), the transmission angle there, and the fraction of perpendicularly polarized power that reflects.
steps: Only about 15% of the perpendicular part reflects, and none of the parallel part, so the reflected light is fully polarized.

problems.title: Both polarizations at 30 degrees
problems.prompt: A plane wave in air hits a dielectric with $\varepsilon_r=4$ at $\theta_i=30^\circ$. Find $\theta_t$, then $\Gamma$, $\tau$, $R$ and $T$ for both perpendicular and parallel polarization.
steps: The parallel component reflects less: it is heading toward its Brewster angle of 63.4°.

problems.title: Glare off a lake
problems.prompt: Unpolarized sunlight (equal perpendicular and parallel power) hits a lake ($n=1.33$) at the Brewster angle. Find the angle, and the fraction of the total incident power that reflects. Which polarization is it?
hints: Each polarization carries half the incident power.
steps: The reflected glare is all perpendicular, which is horizontal for a flat lake, so vertically polarized sunglasses block it.
